text:
mira_support: escalation from customer ACME corp — multiple sporadic 502s and a few 504s on hosted inference calls since ~08:12 UTC. They see failures mostly on short chat sessions (2-6 tokens) after a billing write spike. example req ids: req=acme-7b9c, req=acme-7bd0. :warning:

june_cs: customer says errors started right after they hit a usage threshold and billing backend had increased latency. They reproduced with an empty-context quick generate call. sending their curl below.

mira_support: reproduction curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.host/v1/generate 
 -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED" 
 -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
 -d '{"model":"rwd-small","input":"hi","max_tokens":2}'
```

mira_support: response sometimes returns HTTP/1.1 502 "upstream connect error or disconnect" and body: `{"error":{"message":"upstream error","code":502}}`. other times 504 after ~30s.

sam_eng-sre: :eyes: looking at edge logs now. correlating req ids - I see `upstream_reset` events from midproxy -> billing-proxy cluster at ~08:12:15 and 08:16:02. There are spikes in `queue_length` metric for midfront-auth from 0 -> 350 over ~20s.

alex_runtime: that queue spike smells like authz backpressure (blocking billing calls) causing connection pool exhaustion toward billing. Are these requests authenticated as guest (short token) or tenant keys?

june_cs: ACME says most failing calls are guest sessions (no tenant header) and short requests used in quick UI pings.

sam_eng-sre: confirmed - client_type=guest in traces. midproxy is opening many short-lived streams; h2 keepalive pools low and we get connection churn. Also a pattern of `502` when billing writes exceed 200ms and midfront tries to fanout to billing-sync before responding.

mira_support: attaching sample trace snippet: 
```
[08:12:15] midfront: recv req=req=acme-7b9c size=480 conn_id=23
[08:12:15] midfront: auth->billing call start trace=bf4a
[08:12:16] billing-proxy: write latency=210ms status=200 id=pay-992
[08:12:16] midfront: upstream_reset to billing-proxy reason=pool_exhausted
[08:12:16] midfront: return 502 to client req=acme-7b9c
```

alex_runtime: two quick mitigations to try: 1) temporarily increase midfront h2 conn pool size / keepalive for guest class, 2) short-circuit non-blocking billing validation for very short calls (feature flag). Both require config change on infra side.

sam_eng-sre: agree. also we should add more granular logging around billing write latencies and midfront queue length. I'll push a low-risk config bump: +50 connections for guest pool on midfront for eu1 region.

mira_support: customer is requesting workaround ASAP; can we tell them to reduce parallelism client-side? they have a quick-retry loop with concurrency 8.

june_cs: confirmed, asking them to lower concurrency to 2 and add retry backoff for 1 minute. they can also pin to a dedicated route we provide (non-blocking) but that requires account change.

sam_eng-sre: rolling `midfront.guest_pool_size: +50` on eu1 canary now. Deploy-bot: started rollout to midfront-eu1 (canary id: can-482).

deploy-bot: canary succeeded on 3/3 hosts. monitoring queue_length and downstream errors.

sam_eng-sre: post-patch telemetry: queue_length peak reduced from 350 -> 120, 502s for trace sample dropped to 0 in canary subset. Still seeing occasional 504s with billing latency >1s.

alex_runtime: for longer term: propose (a) make billing calls async for ephemeral guest pings, (b) introduce local KV cache for recent billing decisions (10s TTL), (c) circuit-breaker that falls back to best-effort guest allow when billing is slow. Filing RFC.

mira_support: notes to customer: temporary mitigation applied (guest pool bump), please reduce client concurrency to 2 and enable retry jitter. Eng team investigating async billing path and cache. We'll follow up with an ETA. :thumbsup:

june_cs: owner for customer comms. action items: Sam -> validate rollouts and collect 24h error delta; Alex -> RFC for async billing + cache; Mira -> update support ticket and include sample curl and recommended client changes.

sam_eng-sre: adding links to dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.host/d/midfront/guest-pool?orgId=1&var-region=eu1 and logs for req=acme-7b9c https://logs.redwood.host/trace/acme-7b9c

mira_support: will loop back when RFC lands. closing thread for now, re-open if customer still sees >1% failure after 10m. :white_check_mark:
